text:
Sasha: Heads up — noticed a ~32% throughput drop and intermittent GPU memory spikes on the NF4 canary we rolled yesterday. Affected traffic slice: canary-nf4-3 (~5% requests). Latency P95 up from 180ms -> 260ms and GPU mem spikes +1.2GB. :eyes:
Raj: Which kernel path is the runtime picking? NF4 should route to the 4-bit fast kernels, but these numbers smell like falling back to a slower path or KV thrash.
Michelle: Saw similar in prod traces earlier this morning but only for long-seq (>1024) requests. Short seq seemed fine.
Sasha: Model: redwood-nf4-base-v2, seq distro skewed due to a single customer test (long chat sessions). Canary config sent these to binning-policy v2.
Henry: Can you paste a scheduler/kern-selection sample? Also any change in batching heuristics yesterday?
Sasha: Pasted the runtime debug log here (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-17T09:21:02Z] select_kernel(model=redwood-nf4-base-v2, seq=1500) => chosen=kernel_4bit_slowpath_nf4 (latency_est=12.4ms)
[2026-03-17T09:21:02Z] batching: picked batch_size=8, coalesced=2, batch_latency_est=98ms
[2026-03-17T09:21:02Z] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.27, eviction_rate=0.13, slab_frag=0.44
[2026-03-17T09:21:02Z] kernel_switch: fallback_to_fp4_kern because quant_profile mismatch
```
Sasha: Note the kernel_switch line — the selection log shows a fallback triggered by quant_profile mismatch for a subset of shards.
Raj: perf-bot, any flame graphs for the 09:20 window?
perf-bot: Collected stack samples (09:18-09:25). Top hotspots: 1) 4bit_slowpath_conv (42%), 2) kv_cache_eviction (18%), 3) kernel_selector_lock (12%). Link: http://perf.internal/fg/1938765432
Olivia: kv_cache_eviction at 18% + slab fragmentation 0.44 — that aligns with the +1.2GB spike (GC/eviction churn). Could be the new NF4 binning changed key locality and increased cache misses.
Michelle: Also saw a pattern where batching heuristics create "lockstep": batches for long-seq requests align and push KV prefetch windows out of phase, so we get bursts of misses. I replicated locally by forcing seq=1500 and sending steady QPS.
Henry: Repro steps? I can run microbench on dedicated node.
Michelle: Repro gist: send 12 concurrent clients with seq=1500, inter-arrival jitter 5-15ms. With binning-policy v2 we see throughput oscillation (8 -> 5 -> 9 rps) and KV eviction spikes. With binning-policy v1 it steadies at ~9 rps.
Sasha: Attached sampling perf trace and mini flame: https://artifacts.internal/sasha/nf4-canary-trace-1938765432.svg
Raj: Hypothesis: calibration produced slightly different scale/zero params for a fraction of layers -> kernel_selector sees incompatible quant profile and routes those shards to a safe but slower kernel (4bit_slowpath) which lacks the optimized conv/kernels. That slower kernel increases per-token time and also keeps KV entries alive longer causing fragmentation + evictions.
Olivia: Agree. Also the batching heuristic expects a homogeneous kernel latency; mixing fast and slow kernels in same batch increases tail and can push memory pressure.
perf-bot: Telemetry summary for canary-nf4-3 (last 24h): throughput -28%, avg token latency +43%, kv_hit_rate -12%, kernel_fallback_rate 7.2%.
Sasha: Immediate actions I propose: 1) revert binning-policy v2 for canary-nf4-3 (rollback now), 2) run targeted microbench for mixed-kernel batches and measure memory churn, 3) add selector guard to avoid mixing kernel variants in same physical batch (temporary), 4) re-run calibration sweep with per-layer tolerance and record quant_profile hashes for selector.
Raj: I can own #2 and #3. Will instrument kernel_selector to expose per-batch kernel homogeneity metric and emit histograms.
Michelle: I'll run the calibration sweep with stricter layerwise thresholds and upload deltas.
Henry: I'll file a quick canary revert PR and a follow-up canary with the selector-guard flag off by default.
Sasha: Thanks. If we confirm fallback_rate > 1% triggers instability, we should fail canary promotion automatically. For now I'm reverting. Will post revert ts. :thumbsup:
Olivia: Also recommend adding a KV prefetch jitter to batching heuristic to avoid lockstep alignments — small randomized offset reduces simultaneous eviction pressure (we have prior infra for jittering prefetch).
Sasha: Good call. Add that to follow-up work.
perf-bot: Action checklist created: PERF-4821 (revert), PERF-4822 (mixed-kernel microbench), PERF-4823 (selector telemetry), PERF-4824 (calib-sweep stricter).
Sasha: Closing thread after revert. Will update when microbench results in.
Henry: Revert PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/merge_requests/4512 — rolled back canary at 2026-03-17T09:35:40Z.
Sasha: Reopen if you see reoccurrence after revert. Thanks all. :pray:
